			<font style="display:inline;">For 2016, the benefit for income taxes of $15.4 million related to current tax from operations of $1.1 million, which is primarily the result of revenue withholding taxes paid in foreign tax jurisdictions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The current tax expense was fully offset by a reversal of the valuation allowance of the deferred tax asset that pertains to our net operating loss carryforwards in the United States and changes in certain deferred tax items in foreign entities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on all available evidence, we recorded a tax benefit of $16.5 million for tax attribute carryforwards in the jurisdictions in which there is sufficient positive evidence that the deferred tax asset will be realized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has not provided for U.S. income taxes or foreign withholding taxes on the undistributed earnings of $25.7 million from operations of its subsidiaries operating outside of the United States. Such undistributed earnings are considered permanently reinvested. The Company does not provide deferred taxes on translation adjustments on unremitted earnings under the indefinite reversal exception. Determination of the amount of unrecognized deferred tax liability related to these earnings is not practicable due the complexities of a hypothetical calculation.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">For 2015, the benefit for income taxes of $4.0 million related to current tax from foreign operations of $1.5 million, primarily the result of revenue withholding taxes paid in foreign tax jurisdictions.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2015 current tax expense from foreign operations includes $0.7 million related to a foreign tax receivable that was expensed as collectability was no longer deemed probable.&nbsp;&nbsp;The current tax expense was fully offset by a partial reversal of the valuation allowance of the deferred tax asset that pertains to our net operating loss carryforwards in the United States and changes in certain deferred tax items and current tax obligations in foreign entities. Based on all available evidence, the Company recorded a tax benefit of $6.2&nbsp;million for tax attribute carryforwards in the jurisdictions in which there is sufficient positive evidence that the deferred tax asset will be realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the deferred tax expense from outside the United States includes an expense of $0.5 million related to the reversal of a previously deferred tax asset as the Company determined that the deferred tax asset will not be utilized and the impact on current and prior years accounts are immaterial.<font style="display:inline;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font> &nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For 2014, the provision for income taxes of $0.8 million related primarily to foreign entities. The Company has tax carryforwards in its federal, state and foreign jurisdictions. Based on all available evidence, it was not more likely than not that the Company would realize the benefit from $29.9&nbsp;million of the deferred tax assets. Therefore, a valuation allowance of $28.5&nbsp;million was recorded, which takes into account a deferred tax liability of $0.7&nbsp;million. The Company has recorded a tax benefit for tax attribute carryforwards in the jurisdictions in which there is sufficient positive evidence that the deferred tax asset will be realized, resulting in a net deferred tax asset of $0.7&nbsp;million.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">With few exceptions, the statute of limitations for the years 2012 and prior has expired. Earlier years related to certain foreign jurisdictions remain subject to examination.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, to the extent allowed by law, the tax authorities may have the right to examine prior periods where net operating losses were generated and carried forward, and may make adjustments up to the amount of the net operating loss carryforward. As of December 31, 2016 and 2015, the Company has no significant uncertain tax positions and, therefore, has not recorded any significant liabilities, interest or penalties for uncertain tax positions. To the extent that the Company records any interest or penalties, these amounts will be recorded as part of the income tax provision. If the Company&#x2019;s positions are sustained by the taxing authorities, there will be no impact to the Company&#x2019;s income tax provision.&nbsp;&nbsp;The federal income tax return for the year 2013 is under examination by the Internal Revenue Service.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not believe that there will be any additional tax due.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2016, the Company has available federal net operating loss carryforwards of $56.8&nbsp;million, the most significant of which expire from 2024 through 2033.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6.6pt 0pt 0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">We recognize deferred tax assets and liabilities for future tax consequences arising from differences between the carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities under GAAP and their respective tax basis, and for net operating loss carryforwards and tax credit carryforwards. We evaluate the recoverability of our deferred tax assets, weighing all positive and negative evidence, and are required to establish or maintain a valuation allowance for these assets if we determine that it is more likely than not that some or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. The weight given to the evidence is commensurate with the extent to which the evidence can be objectively verified. If negative evidence exists, positive evidence is necessary to support a conclusion that a valuation allowance is not needed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Our framework for assessing the recoverability of deferred tax assets requires us to weigh all available evidence, including:</font>

After weighing all of the evidence, we determined that the positive evidence in favor of releasing a portion of the valuation allowance outweighed the negative evidence against releasing the allowance as of December 31, 2016. Therefore, we concluded that it was more likely than not that our deferred tax assets, relating primarily to net operating loss carryforwards&nbsp;in the United States, would be realized. As a result, we released $19.6 million of the valuation allowance on our deferred tax assets as of December 31, 2016.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">14. Retirement plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">All U.S. employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan which covers U.S. employees meeting certain age requirements in accordance with section&nbsp;401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code. Under the provisions of the 401(k) plan, the Company has the ability to make matching contributions equal to a percentage of the employee&#x2019;s voluntary contribution, as well as a non&#8209;elective contribution. From the inception of the 401(k) plan the Company has not made a contribution of any type.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">15. Segment information</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">General information</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The segment and geographic information provided in the table below is being reported consistent with the Company&#x2019;s method of internal reporting. Operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise for which separate financial information is available and which is evaluated regularly by the chief operating decision maker (&#x201C;CODM&#x201D;) in deciding how to allocate resources and in assessing performance. The CODM reviews net revenue and gross profit by service by geographical region. The Company operates in two reportable segments; multi&#8209;currency processing services and payment processing services.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Information about revenue, profit and assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The CODM evaluates performance and allocates resources based on net revenue and gross profit of each segment. For purposes of analyzing segments, gross profit of the multi&#8209;currency processing services segment is equal to net revenue less multi&#8209;currency cost of sales of $2.3 million, $3.7 million and $2.0 million, which is included in &#x201C;processing and services costs&#x201D; for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2016, 2015 and 2014, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The gross profit for the payment processing services segment includes net revenue of the segment less the cost of revenue component &#x201C;payment processing services fees,&#x201D; which includes interchange and card network fees and assessments. Net revenue and gross profit by geographical region is based upon where the transaction originated. Lastly, the Company does not evaluate performance or allocate resources using segment asset data. Long-lived assets are primarily located in the Americas and Europe and as of December&nbsp;31, 2016 and December&nbsp;31, 2015, long&#8209;lived asset amounts are $7.0 million and $7.4 million, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company conducts its business primarily in three geographical regions: Asia Pacific (&#x201C;APAC&#x201D;), the Americas, and Europe, Middle East and Africa (&#x201C;EMEA&#x201D;). The following table provides revenue concentration by geographic region. </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">16. Stock repurchase program</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In 2014 and 2015, the Board of Directors authorized a total repurchase of $13.5 million of the Company&#x2019;s outstanding shares of common stock and repurchased a total amount of 3.6 million shares of common stock for an aggregate price of $7.9 million as of December 31, 2015. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">From January 1, 2016 to March 9, 2016, the Company repurchased an additional 1.3 million shares under the program for an aggregate price of $3.6 million, thus $2.0 million remained available for repurchase under the program.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of March 10, 2016, the stock repurchase program was suspended in connection with the tender offer (see disclosure below). On August 2, 2016, the Board of Directors reinstated the Company&#x2019;s share repurchase program and expanded the authorization by an incremental $4.0 million, bringing its total authorization to $6.0 million. From August 2, 2016 to September 30, 2016, the Company repurchased approximately 1.6 million shares of common stock for an aggregate price of $6.0 million. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">On November 1, 2016, the Company announced that its Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $10.0 million of the Company&#x2019;s outstanding shares of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;From October 1, 2016 through the date of this filing, the Company did not repurchase any shares of common stock.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Tender offer</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">On March 10, 2016, the Board of Directors authorized the Company to commence a modified &#x201C;Dutch auction&#x201D; tender offer to repurchase up to $15.0 million of its outstanding shares of common stock at a tender price of not less than $3.20 per share or greater than $3.60 per share. The tender offer commenced on March 14, 2016 and expired on April 11, 2016. On April 12, 2016, the Company paid $14.2 million, including transaction costs, to repurchase approximately 3.9 million shares at a tender price of $3.60 per share. The repurchased shares of common stock became treasury shares of the Company.</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We carried out an evaluation under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures, as such term is defined in Rules&nbsp;13a&#8209;15(e) and 15d&#8209;15(e) under the Exchange Act. In designing and evaluating our disclosure controls and procedures, we and our management recognize that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving the desired control objectives, and our management necessarily was required to apply its judgment in evaluating and implementing possible controls and procedures. Based upon that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on form&nbsp;10&#8209;K, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting during the quarter ended December&nbsp;31, 2016, which were identified in connection with management&#x2019;s evaluation required by paragraph&nbsp;(d) of Rules&nbsp;13a&#8209;15(f) and 15d&#8209;15(f) under the Exchange Act, that might have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Management&#x2019;s Annual Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Rules&nbsp;13a&#8209;15(f) and 15d&#8209;15(f) under the Exchange Act. Our internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. In addition, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions and that the degree of compliance with policies or procedures may deteriorate. Management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2016. In making this assessment, management used the criteria set forth in the Internal Control&#x2014; Integrated Framework (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Based on its assessment of internal control over financial reporting, our CEO and CFO have concluded that, as of December&nbsp;31, 2016, our internal control over financial reporting was effective. Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Therefore, even those systems determined to be effective can provide only assurance at a reasonable level with respect to the financial statement preparation and presentation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">This annual report does not include an attestation report of the Company&#x2019;s independent registered public accounting firm regarding internal control over financial reporting due to a transition period established by the rules of the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act for newly public companies.</font>
		</p>
